Director, Enterprise Applications

Office of the Chief Information Officer, Corporate Services

Be bold. Think bigger. Create lasting impact.

At Peel Region, technology enables the essential public services our communities rely on every day.

Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director, Enterprise Applications
will shape Peel’s enterprise technology direction and lead the modernization and sustainable operation of critical platforms, including SAP S/4HANA, SAP Concur and IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management.

This is an opportunity to lead meaningful business transformation and strengthen systems supporting approximately 7,000 users across Peel Region.

The opportunity

You will connect technology investments with Peel’s strategic priorities, service outcomes and future needs. Working with senior leaders, business teams and external partners, you will lead enterprise application strategy, major implementations, governance, operational sustainment and organizational adoption.

Your leadership will ensure Peel’s enterprise applications are integrated, reliable and positioned to deliver lasting value for employees, services and the community.

Advancing Peel’s strategic priorities

Peel’s Strategic Plan Sets The Direction For Building a Community For Life
. This Role Will Contribute Particularly To Service Excellence, Our People And Future Ready
By:

Modernizing the systems that enable essential public services.
Improving the technology experience for employees and leaders.
Strengthening data, reporting and enterprise decision-making.
Establishing sustainable application support and governance models.
Supporting responsible stewardship of public resources.
Helping employees successfully adopt new technology and ways of working.

Learn more about the Peel Region Strategic Plan .

What You Will Do

Lead Peel’s Enterprise Applications Strategy and Roadmap.
Provide strategic leadership for SAP S/4HANA, SAP Concur, IBM Maximo and other critical enterprise applications.
Oversee complex implementation, modernization, integration and sustainment initiatives.
Align technology investments with service priorities, user needs and measurable organizational benefits.
Establish governance, service standards, service-level agreements and sustainable support models.
Maintain stable operations while leading the transition to modern solutions.
Lead organizational change through stakeholder engagement, business readiness, communications, training and adoption.
Manage procurement, implementation partners, strategic suppliers, contracts, budgets, deliverables and vendor performance.
Identify enterprise risks, resolve complex issues and provide clear advice to senior leaders.
Build trusted relationships across business and technology functions.
Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team that values accountability, collaboration and professional growth.

What You Bring

A relevant postgraduate degree, preferably in Business, Computer Science, Information Technology or a related discipline.
SAP Certified Application Associate and/or SAP Certified Development Associate certification.
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
At least eight years of experience implementing enterprise applications in a complex public-sector environment.
A satisfactory Level 2 Criminal Record Check obtained directly from a police station (third-party background checks will not be accepted).
Implementation and operational experience with SAP S/4HANA and SAP Concur and/or IBM Maximo Enterprise Asset Management.
Experience leading large-scale technology implementations across multiple business functions and stakeholder groups.
Strong knowledge and practical application of formal project management methodologies.
Experience managing procurement, implementation partners, contracts, budgets, deliverables and vendor performance.
Experience establishing governance, service standards, service-level agreements and operational support models.
Strong strategic thinking, change leadership, risk management and relationship-building skills.
An understanding of government structures, political considerations and Council-level accountability.

How You Will Demonstrate Peel’s Values

Inclusion: Engage diverse perspectives to create accessible, user-centred enterprise solutions.
Transparency: Establish clear governance and communicate openly about decisions, progress, risks, costs and results.
Care and Support: Lead change with empathy and help employees confidently adopt new technology.
Collaboration: Bring business, technology and external partners together around shared outcomes.
Leadership: Set a clear direction, make accountable decisions, develop people and champion innovation and continuous improvement.

Why work at Peel?

At Peel, you can lead, impact and grow
while helping shape better communities and build a Community for Life
.

You Will Join An Inclusive And Values-led Organization Where Employees Are Encouraged To Be Bold, Think Bigger And Contribute Meaningfully. In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To:

Shape Peel’s enterprise applications strategy and future technology roadmap.
Lead transformation across critical business platforms.
Influence decisions that strengthen services and organizational performance.
Improve the technology experience for employees and leaders.
Develop people and build future organizational capability.
Make a lasting contribution to responsive and sustainable public service.

The Peel Employee Experience

As an eligible employee, you will receive:

Comprehensive health, dental and vision benefits, including psychological health supports, effective on your first day.
Automatic enrolment in the OMERS pension plan.
Five weeks of annual vacation accrued monthly.
Three paid personal days, in addition to floating holidays.
Flexible work hours that support well-being and work-life integration.
An inclusive workplace culture grounded in collaborative leadership and meaningful public service.

Join us.

Enterprise applications are more than technology platforms. They enable our employees, strengthen public services and help Peel respond to changing community needs.

Bring your experience, perspective and leadership to Peel and help shape the future of technology-enabled public service.

In this role, you’ll benefit from the flexibility of a hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes meaningful in-person connection. A minimum of two days per week on-site
is expected, with additional in-person presence as operational needs evolve. This arrangement allows for a blend of in person and hybrid work that adapts to support both organizational priorities and employee flexibility and is subject to change over time.

It's important to note that your off-site work location must be within the province of Ontario. This ensures that we're compliant with all regulations and policies.

The Region of Peel offers job based flexible hours of work that allows employees to manage personal and professional responsibilities while at the same time ensures business operational needs and customer service expectations are achieved.

Peel Region consists of the cities of Brampton and Mississauga, and the town of Caledon. Peel Region delivers essential services to more than 1.5 million residents and approximately 200,000 businesses.

We’re working to create a community that is safe, inclusive, and accessible. A place where everyone feels they belong and can access the services they need to thrive throughout each stage of life.

Our workforce is 6,700 strong and s ince 1974, we’ve been delivering a wide range of resident focused services. Our services include paramedic services, health programs, long-term care and services for seniors, child care support, garbage collection and recycling, waste water and water treatment, road maintenance, financial assistance, and housing support.

Recognized by Canada's Healthy Workplace Month® with the Great Employer Award

We strive to develop a workplace that values and respects diversity, practices inclusion, recognizes the unique contributions and abilities of all people and facilitates innovative thinking. At Peel Region, people come first. Each employee has an important role within our community and when we work together, it’s impactful. We encourage you to join us in delivering essential services and programs to our diverse community. You won't find a better opportunity than Peel Region.

About Us

At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong, dedicated network of supports and staff to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity

Financial leadership in OSD has a direct connection to the programs, services and external providers that support Nova Scotians. As Director of Finance, you will lead a complex, province-wide financial operation and help ensure that leaders have the accurate information, practical advice and effective controls needed to make responsible decisions.

This is an opportunity to combine professional accounting expertise with broader leadership. You will guide financial operations, strengthen planning and risk management, support sound decision-making, and lead a sizeable team through competing priorities and organizational change. Your success will depend not only on technical knowledge, but also on your judgement, communication, relationship-building, and ability to help others deliver results.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you have the opportunity to lead a substantial finance function, advise senior decision-makers and improve the systems and practices that support programs and services across Nova Scotia. A few of your key responsibilities are to:

Provide strategic and operational financial advice to the Executive Director and senior leaders, translating complex financial and non-financial information into clear options, risks and recommendations.
Lead the delivery and continuous improvement of financial operations that support departmental programs, regional teams and external service providers.
Provide leadership for budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of cost pressures, helping leaders make informed choices about resources and program delivery.
Strengthen financial accountability through effective internal controls, risk management, transparent reporting and compliance with applicable accounting standards and government financial policies.
Lead, support and develop a geographically distributed finance team. Set clear direction, build management capability, encourage collaboration and create the conditions for people to take ownership of their work.
Provide clear direction and leadership to managers and staff by establishing priorities, clarifying accountabilities, delegating effectively and supporting consistent delivery across the finance function.
Build the capability and resilience of the finance team through workforce planning, coaching, performance management and succession development.
Exercise sound professional judgment and critical thinking in interpreting and applying provincial government financial policies and applicable accounting standards within complex and diverse contexts, considering both financial and non-financial information.
Build productive relationships across OSD and with central agencies, internal audit, legal partners, service providers and other stakeholders. Address difficult issues with diplomacy while maintaining professional standards and public accountability.
Lead practical improvements to financial processes, systems and service delivery. Sequence change thoughtfully so that essential operations remain stable and responsive.
Represent the department on relevant cross-government initiatives, committees and working groups, and communicate financial issues clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a designated Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) with progressively responsible experience leading financial operations and people in a complex organization. Your experience demonstrates that you can:

lead managers and professional staff in a complex work environment, including setting expectations, delegating responsibility, developing capability and addressing performance concerns.
assess workforce and organizational needs, strengthen team capacity and guide employees through operational or organizational change while maintaining service delivery.
prepare and deliver briefings or presentations for executive-level audiences, including providing credible financial advice and explaining complex issues
support budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of significant or competing financial pressures;
establish or strengthen internal controls, accountability and risk-management practices;
build effective relationships and resolve difficult issues with sound judgement, discretion and diplomacy; and
organize work, adapt to changing priorities and deliver accurate advice within tight timeframes.

You bring a practical understanding of professional accounting standards and the ability to apply financial policy in a complex operating environment. You also understand that strong financial management requires attention to program and service outcomes, not only financial results.

The Following Experience Would Be Considered An Asset

audit, assurance or control-review work;
public-sector, human-services, not-for-profit or other complex service-delivery finance;
financial relationships with funded organizations, service providers, grants or contribution agreements;
Public Sector Accounting Standards and government financial policy

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions

Your typical work week is 35 hours with 7-hour days. The role includes regular travel to regional offices and other work sites across Nova Scotia.

jobs.description:
Come make your difference in communities across Canada, where authenticity, trust and making connections is valued – as we shape the future of Canadian retail, together. Our unique position as one of the country's largest employers, coupled with our commitment to positively impact the lives of all Canadians, provides our colleagues a range of opportunities and experiences to help Canadians Live Life Well®.

At Loblaw Companies Limited, we succeed through collaboration and commitment and set a high bar for ourselves and those around us. Whether you are just starting your career, re-entering the workforce, or looking for a new job, this is where you belong.

As the Senior Director, Sourcing Analytics, you will lead the development of a best-in-class analytics function that strengthens commercial decision-making, accelerates value creation and transforms the capabilities of Loblaw's Sourcing organization. Reporting to the SVP, Enterprise Sourcing, you will serve as a strategic advisor to the Chief Sourcing Officer and Sourcing Leadership, bringing together deep analytical expertise and commercial judgment to shape critical sourcing decisions and advance enterprise performance.

At the heart of this mandate is ownership of Category Analytics, Sourcing data and reporting, advanced analytics, and the Sourcing AI capability roadmap. You will establish the analytical standards, data foundations and scalable tools that enable category teams to execute sophisticated sourcing strategies, evaluate supplier economics and negotiate with greater confidence. Working across Fresh and CoS/HABA, you will ensure that insights translate into practical, high-impact commercial recommendations.

You will also lead the evolution of Sourcing's analytical and AI-enabled capabilities, partnering with Digital, Technology and Strategy & Value Delivery to bring new solutions into the business. Combining enterprise leadership, commercial acumen and a commitment to innovation, you will play a pivotal role in advancing our ambition to be the World's Best Buyers.

Core Responsibilities

Category Analytics & Commercial Value Creation

Lead the Category Analytics function across Fresh and CoS/HABA, setting the analytical agenda and standards for the highest-impact sourcing decisions and commercial opportunities.
Oversee sophisticated Fresh sourcing events, including complex RFP design, bid evaluation and award scenarios; and CoS/HABA supplier plays, offer assessments and negotiation analytics.
Challenge commercial assumptions, quantify alternative scenarios and develop recommendations that strengthen negotiation strategies, supplier decisions and enterprise value.
Partner with Sourcing and Merchandising leaders to prioritize analytical resources against the most material category opportunities and measure the impact of resulting decisions.

Sourcing Data, Reporting & Performance Intelligence

Own the Sourcing data and analytics agenda, defining priorities for data quality, accessibility, governance and effective use in commercial and strategic decision-making.
Establish enterprise-consistent Sourcing performance metrics, executive dashboards and analytical reporting that provide clear visibility into sourcing effectiveness, supplier performance and emerging opportunities.
Partner with Enterprise Data, Finance and Technology teams to strengthen data foundations, clarify ownership and controls, and connect internal and external sources into decision-ready insights.
Evolve reporting from retrospective measurement toward forward-looking insight, predictive analysis and actionable commercial intelligence.

Advanced Analytics & AI Capability Transformation

Own and lead the multi-year Sourcing advanced analytics and AI capability roadmap, defining the highest-value use cases, business requirements, investment priorities and measures of success.
Champion the development and deployment of advanced models, automation, Generative AI and emerging agentic capabilities that improve sourcing decisions, negotiations and colleague productivity.
Partner with Digital, Technology and enterprise analytics teams to guide solution design, testing, data readiness and responsible implementation, ensuring capabilities are scalable and fit for business use.
Work with Strategy & Value Delivery, which leads organizational adoption and ways-of-working change, to connect new capabilities to measurable operational and financial outcomes.

Executive Partnership & Enterprise Influence

Translate sophisticated analyses into clear executive narratives, recommendations and trade-offs, with a focus on enterprise rather than isolated category outcomes.
Collaborate across Sourcing, Merchandising, Finance, Commodity & Business Intelligence, Digital and Technology to align complementary insights and avoid duplication of accountabilities.

Team Leadership & Capability Building

Build, lead and develop a high-performing team of Category Analytics professionals, setting clear expectations for commercial impact, analytical rigour, quality and stakeholder partnership.
Establish reusable analytical methodologies, models and tools while enabling the category-specific approaches required for Fresh and CoS/HABA.
Develop talent and a culture of curiosity, continuous improvement and AI-enabled ways of working, strengthening analytical capability across the wider Sourcing organization.
Key Skills and Qualifications:
10+ years of progressive experience in sourcing, procurement, merchandising, commercial analytics, strategy or related fields, including significant experience leading teams and complex cross-functional initiatives.
Proven record of influencing material commercial decisions and delivering value through sophisticated sourcing analytics, supplier economics, negotiation support and executive-level recommendations.
Demonstrated ownership of enterprise data, reporting or advanced analytics capabilities, including data governance, performance measurement and scalable analytical solutions.
Experience shaping and delivering analytics or AI transformation roadmaps in partnership with business and technology stakeholders; ability to evaluate opportunities pragmatically and manage implementation risks.
Exceptional commercial judgment, structured problem-solving, executive communication and ability to influence senior leaders in a complex matrixed organization.
Knowledge of relevant analytics and visualization tools and familiarity with modern data and AI capabilities; ability to lead technical specialists without needing to be the hands-on developer
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Computer Science or related discipline; MBA or other relevant advanced degree an asset.

jobs.description:
SUNPAN is a fast-growing global furniture brand that specializes in the design of high quality, trend-forward furnishings for commercial and residential spaces. We collaborate with established designers and suppliers from around the globe to source the finest materials and inspired styles. As a trade-only company, we are a trusted source for interior designers seeking timeless pieces that elevate any space. Our curated assortment spans across dining and bar to living, bedroom, outdoor, and accents.

Proudly certified as a Great Place to Work for five consecutive years, SUNPAN fosters a creative and supportive environment. We welcome talented individuals to explore rewarding career opportunities across our diverse teams.

Job Summary

Sunpan is looking for a hands-on technology leader for our technology and digital transformation strategy. The Director will define how we structure, grow and continuously improve our IT function, guide the implementation of business systems, and lead our innovation, AI and automation strategy in line with the organization's priorities.

Technology is central to how Sunpan grows, and this role sets its direction. Working side by side with the executive team, you will decide where we invest, how the IT function is organized and which tools and ideas help us work smarter. You will build on a focused team and shape it into a function the whole business relies on.

About The Role

Technology Leadership and Team Building

Lead, mentor and develop the IT team, and recommend the roles, structure and skills needed as the department grows.
Establish a roadmap and operating model for IT that supports continuous improvement, reliability and scalability.
Manage vendors, service providers and consultants, including contracts, performance and budgets.
Design and build the core IT infrastructure and architecture, including enterprise systems, integrations, networks, security and support, that will serve as the backbone for Sunpan’s growth.

Strategy, Innovation and Business Cases

Lead the development and execution of an innovation, technology, AI and automation strategy aligned with organizational priorities.
Identify and evaluate emerging technologies and digital solutions that improve operations, efficiency and overall performance.
Prepare business cases, ROI analyses and recommendations for the executive team to support technology investments.

Systems Implementation and Optimization

Serve as the lead and escalation point for enterprise system implementations and upgrades, from requirements through go-live and adoption.
Own the SAP landscape strategy, working with the business analyst, functional leads and implementation partners.
Oversee and integrate other core business platforms, including HubSpot (CRM and marketing), warehouse management systems (WMS) and EDI.
Improve workflows across sales, supply chain, warehousing, finance and customer service through process redesign, integration and automation.
Oversee the technology project portfolio, including planning, prioritization, resourcing, timelines, budgets and status reporting to the executive team.

AI and Digital Adoption

Lead AI and digital transformation initiatives from concept to implementation, partnering with business leaders, technical teams and end users.
Identify where AI can enhance efficiency and deliver measurable value.
Drive adoption through training, change management, communication and user engagement.

Governance, Security and Risk

Establish policies, standards and governance practices for IT and the responsible use of AI.
Establish governance for the IT function, including vendor and contract management, technology budgets, financial reporting, and resource allocation.
Identify and manage technology-related risks across the organization, including cybersecurity, privacy, and information security.
Ensure technology aligns with cybersecurity, privacy and information management policies.
Support technology risk management, business continuity and compliance requirements.

Let's Talk About You

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Business or a related field (or equivalent experience).
10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years in a leadership role.
Strong, hands-on SAP experience, including implementation, support and integration.
Experience managing technology vendors and contracts, and allocating budgets and resources across a portfolio of projects
Proven track record leading enterprise system implementations from planning through adoption.
Experience with HubSpot, warehouse management systems and EDI in a supply chain, wholesale or distribution environment.
Demonstrated ability to build business cases and present to executives.
Working knowledge of cybersecurity, privacy and IT governance frameworks.
Excellent communication, change management and stakeholder management skills.
Experience working with consulting groups, architecture firms or other project-based professional services companies.
Practical experience applying artificial intelligence, automation and enterprise technology to improve business processes.
Experience developing technology roadmaps, security and governance frameworks and policies, and implementation plans, with strong project management skills.

Preferred

Deep SAP expertise, plus hands-on experience with HubSpot and warehouse management systems.
Experience in furniture, consumer goods, retail or import/distribution.
Practical experience deploying AI and automation tools in a business setting.
Experience building or restructuring an IT department in a small-to-mid-sized company.
Relevant certifications (e.g., PMP, ITIL, SAP, CISSP or CISM).

Job Description

About Agilent

Agilent is a global leader in laboratory and clinical technologies, we are passionate about bringing great science to life. We help scientists, researchers, and clinicians address some of the world’s most important challenges across life science research, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, food, environmental testing, and related markets.

Leveraging more than 50 years of expertise, we develop advanced instruments, software, consumables, and services that enable customers to generate reliable scientific results and improve scientific, economic, and operational outcomes. Our global organization combines deep technical expertise with a commitment to quality, innovation, and customer impact. We work collaboratively with our customers on their journey to make a real difference in human lives. Our culture is founded on trust, respect, and uncompromising integrity, and we pride ourselves on being a dynamic and inclusive workplace that empowers employees and fosters innovation.

The Role

Agilent is seeking a highly experienced product strategy leader to help define how laboratories will evolve over the next five to ten years and translate that vision into actionable strategies for our businesses and product organizations.

This senior individual contributor works across the enterprise at the intersection of customer insight, science, technology, and business strategy. As a recognized internal expert, you will lead high-impact, long-range initiatives, advise senior leadership, and independently solve complex challenges spanning multiple functions with limited support. You will connect external signals and customer needs with business-group priorities, product roadmaps, and execution.

Key Responsibilities

Assess how AI, automation, robotics, connected instruments, digital workflows, data platforms, and autonomous experimentation could change laboratory work. Identify practical applications in scientific productivity, instrument operation, workflow optimization, decision support, and service; distinguish durable shifts from short-term technology cycles.
Evaluate new products, solutions, partnerships, and business models. Develop strategic and financial cases that assess customer value, differentiation, and feasibility; recommend when to build, partner, invest, acquire, or apply existing capabilities differently.
Develop and continually refine Agilent’s view of Autonomous Labs. Synthesize scientific, technological, economic, and operational trends, including changing workforce models and productivity pressures, into scenarios and implications for our portfolio, business models, and investments.
Engage scientists, laboratory leaders, executives, key opinion leaders, and strategic customers to understand current operations and emerging needs. Identify workflow bottlenecks, fragmented data, automation gaps, usability challenges, and inefficiencies that span individual instruments or product categories.
Synthesize customer feedback across markets and businesses into clear problem statements, strategic requirements, opportunity areas, and investment recommendations. Connect market direction, competitive developments, technology adoption, and laboratory economics to customer value and business opportunity.
Partner with individual business and product groups to translate enterprise insight into specific decisions about what to develop, accelerate, integrate, redesign, partner around, or stop pursuing. Convert recommendations into product concepts, roadmap changes, customer experiments, and investment cases.
Lead initiatives across product management, R&D, commercial, digital, service, and business leadership. Align teams around customer problems that cross organizational boundaries and opportunities to combine instruments, software, consumables, automation, services, and data into more complete solutions.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a scientific, engineering, business, or related discipline, or equivalent experience. A PhD, MBA, or equivalent advanced experience is strongly preferred.
Typically 12+ years of relevant combined experience across product strategy, product management, scientific research, strategy consulting, operations, technology, business development, or related fields.
Experience in life sciences, analytical instrumentation, diagnostics, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, laboratory technology, or adjacent markets is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to understand complex markets, translate trends into business strategy, and turn customer insight into product, portfolio, or organizational action.
A record of delivering results across functions and working credibly with senior business leaders, scientists, engineers, and product teams.

Skills And Competencies

Strategic and systems thinking, with the ability to recognize patterns across markets, customers, technologies, and businesses.
Scientific and technical fluency, curiosity about AI and automation, and sound product judgment grounded in customer needs.
Structured problem solving and analytical rigor; ability to turn ambiguous information into concrete decisions and priorities.
Executive communication, facilitation, and influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority.
Ability to move between long-range strategy and practical execution, aligning stakeholders and sustaining follow-through.

This job has a full time weekly schedule. It includes the option to work remotely.

Job Description

DePuy Synthes is currently recruiting for a Senior Director, Acquisitions & Divestitures (A&D) Finance to ideally be located in Raynham, MA.

The Corporate A&D Finance team is seeking a seasoned, strategic, and influential Senior Director to serve as the enterprise finance thought partner on portfolio shaping and capital deployment decisions across our sectors (Pharmaceuticals and Medical Technologies). This leader will set the financial point of view behind DePuy Synthes’s acquisitions, partnerships, and divestitures, determining how each transaction fits the enterprise strategy, creates sustainable long-term value, and aligns with capital allocation priorities. The Senior Director will partner with corporate and sector executives, Business Development, the A&D Community of Practice, and external advisors to establish valuation frameworks, challenge key assumptions, and deliver clear, decision-ready recommendations to the most senior leaders of the company (GOC, EC/MC, and Board of Directors).

Johnson & Johnson announced plans to separate our Orthopedics business to establish a standalone orthopedics company, operating as DePuy Synthes. The process of the planned separation is anticipated to be completed within 18 to 24 months, subject to legal requirements, including consultation with works councils and other employee representative bodies, as may be required, regulatory approvals and other customary conditions and approvals. Should you accept this position, it is anticipated that, following conclusion of the transaction, you would be an employee of DePuy Synthes and your employment would be governed by DePuy Synthes employment processes, programs, policies, and benefit plans. In that case, details of any planned changes would be provided to you by DePuy Synthes at an appropriate time and subject to any necessary consultation processes.

Responsibilities

Serve as a strategic finance advisor to enterprise and sector leaders on portfolio strategy, helping shape the pipeline of acquisitions, partnerships, and divestitures so that it reflects long-term growth objectives, capital allocation priorities, and the evolving competitive landscape. Provide an independent, objective perspective that balances opportunity with risk.
Lead and oversee objective financial and business analyses of new acquisitions, partnering relationships (i.e. options, licenses, equity investments, etc.), and divestitures, ensuring objectivity, transparency, and completeness in strategic assessments, valuations, and due diligence (highlighting both opportunities and risks) as well as transaction closing activities (purchase price allocation, deal financings, etc.). Distill complex analyses into clear insights and recommendations for senior management, the GOC, EC/MC, and the Board of Directors.
Provide senior financial leadership across the full deal lifecycle, guiding deal structuring, contract and purchase price negotiations, valuation, due diligence, EC/MC and BOD presentations, Investor Relations support and framing, EPS analyses, and capital structure impacts. Direct the work of deal teams, external advisors, and investment bankers to ensure transactions deliver the intended value.
Oversee the review of key legal documents and required regulatory filings in support of specific transactions, partnering with Legal, Tax, and Controllership to structure transactions that protect value and manage risk.
Own the vision for, and continuously evolve, the enterprise A&D valuation and decision-making framework. Design, develop, enhance, and implement processes that lead to more accurate valuation assessments, drive value creation, and mitigate risk. This includes driving compliance with EC/MC approved Acquisition and Divestiture processes/standards and ensuring that standardized information is reviewed and output templates are used during investment decision-making meetings (consistency cross-sector, cross deal type).
Drive improved acquisition and divestiture outcomes by leading post-transaction reviews that measure results against the original deal thesis, and by translating lessons learned into process improvements and guidance for management and business development partners.
Lead special enterprise projects of a financial nature as required, including, but not limited to capital allocation analytics, share repurchase programs, cost of capital, dividend proposals, J&J and affiliate valuations, capital structure, credit ratings, etc.
Build and sustain influential relationships with key members of the J&J Finance, Business Development, and A&D Community of Practice teams to foster a culture of objectivity, transparency, and constructive dialogue on financial and valuation matters. Act as a trusted advisor to senior executives and be recognized as a J&J Finance leader and thought partner in the M&A and portfolio management discipline. Demonstrate an open and flexible mindset that inspires creative and innovative solutions while maintaining a value creation discipline. This position works closely with other key M&A oriented groups including the following: Sector BD, A&D Operations, Controllership/GTAAS, Tax, Investor Relations, Legal, HR, third party advisors and investment bankers.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree is required, preferably in Finance, Accounting, or other business-related discipline. If undergraduate degree is not in Finance or Accounting, then an MBA in Finance is highly recommended.
CMA, CPA, CFA and/or an MBA is preferred (or its equivalents).
A minimum of 12 years of finance, accounting or related business experience is required.
BU Finance experience (in Commercial/Supply Chain/R&D finance) at the Senior Manager or Director level is preferred.
Experience with Financial Analysis, Financial Valuation Modeling, and Investment decision-making is preferred.
Ability to understand and interrogate all financial statements and their key linkages is required.
Excellent analytical, communication and business partnership skills as well as the ability to lead and collaborate in a highly matrix environment across multiple sectors, regions, and functions.
Demonstrate the ability to challenge the status quo and provide recommendations to enhance value creation opportunities required.
